contents.text:
I'm working out what the page covers: it has four areas, starting with running things on the user's own machine through two Docker stacks, then watching each turn in the Aspire dashboard, then the Azure deploy that ships on every merge. I'll answer briefly and close by offering a few choices.

I'm settling on the answer's shape now: plain paragraphs rather than lists, since lists are reserved for steps and choices. The page is the source, so I don't need to cite anything else, and I'll finish with the three offered choices.

This page shows how to run louis-agent. It covers three things: running it in Docker on your own machine, watching each turn on a dashboard, and how both websites reach Azure on every merge.

The first area starts two Docker stacks. One runs the coding agent and its code-review app. The other runs louis-agent.dev and this site. Every port binds to your own machine only.

The second area starts the Aspire dashboard. Each turn, model request and tool call appears there as a trace, with its logs. It keeps everything in memory, so a restart clears it.

The third area explains deployment. Merging to `main` releases both sites to Azure through GitHub, so your machine doesn't need to be on.
